_comment: The jewellery catalogue. This is the ONLY file to edit when adding or
removing a piece — no JavaScript changes are needed.
To add jewellery:
1. Create a folder under objects/ holding one model file.
2. Add the folder name to the list below.
Supported model formats, in the order they are preferred when a folder
holds more than one:
glb, gltf, obj, stl, ply, fbx, 3ds, dae, 3mf, 3dm
GLB is the best choice: it is the only one built for the web, so it is the
smallest download and carries its materials and textures inside the single
file. STEP, IGES, .blend and .ztl cannot be opened by any browser and have
to be converted first.
Name the file model.<ext> — for example model.glb, model.stl, model.3dm.
scene.<ext> and <folder-name>.<ext> are also found, and OBJ additionally
accepts 1.obj / 2.obj / 3.obj. Any other name will not be found.
An OBJ may have its model.mtl and texture images (.jpg / .png / .webp)
beside it; the other formats carry their materials internally, except STL,
which has none at all and renders as one solid metal.
The short form is just the folder name. The category and the display
label are worked out from it: 'necklace-gold' becomes a Gold Necklace.
Dashes, underscores and spaces all work, the category word may lead or
trail, and plurals are fine — 'Gold_Necklace' and 'earrings-hoop' both
resolve correctly.
Use the long form when the folder name cannot say it for you:
{ "folder": "aurora-set-01", "category": "necklace", "label": "Aurora" }
The long form also takes a "model" field naming the file directly:
{ "folder": "aurora-set-01", "model": "model.glb" }
With it the browser skips probing entirely, which now saves up to thirty
requests per folder.
Supported categories: necklace, earring, ring, bangles.
'bracelet', 'bangle' and 'kada' are all understood as bangles too, so a
folder uploaded under any of those names still works.
A folder listed here with no loadable model shows as unavailable rather
than disappearing, so a missing upload is visible instead of silent.
If this file is absent the app falls back to a built-in list, so nothing
breaks — but a real installation should always generate it.
